rationale: The strongest ecological result, orientation_environment_association_is_scale_partitioned, is already a frozen core result of Chapter 2 rather than unused validation material.
The preregistered external-taxon V1 and source-complete V2 confirmation attempts are not evaluable under strict public occurrence metadata; V2 leaves D=0 and U=1 after QC.
Azami image data are existing non-independent cross-scale evidence and already contain the relevant BIO1/BIO12/BIO15 outcomes.
Phyllary public ecology remains state-replication limited and stickiness has no source-complete external nonsticky comparison.

ecological_core: common9 shows no one shared abiotic niche signature across three historical traits
orientation ecology is scale-partitioned across within-taxon, among-taxon and East-Asian state/transition representations
transition-conditioned BIO15-up/BIO1-down correspondence is positive but history-embedded
historical climate does not identify a persistent origin regime
chapter2_role.headline: mosaic historical assembly with scale-conditioned ecological correspondence
chapter2_role.claim_boundary: not adaptation, direct selection, convergence or historical climatic causation

next_standalone_ecology_paper.central_question: Do capitulum components affect reproductive fitness through distinct ecological pathways rather than one common floral-syndrome mechanism?
causal_chain: wetting + floral microclimate + time-resolved effective pollination + antagonist exposure
